weaknesses: The plan adds substantial evening study on Monday and Tuesday from 19:00 to 21:00 immediately after already long days with morning training, university commitments, afternoon training ending at 18:30, and only a 30-minute gap before study. The rationale says this reaches the study target, but does not really weigh whether those hours are likely to be usable after two-a-day training and classes.

Wednesday is especially compressed before travel: morning taper training 07:00-09:00, university class 10:00-12:00, lunch 12:30-13:30, added study 13:30-14:30, physio at 14:30-15:30, team briefing/light session 16:30-18:30, packing 20:30-21:30, then sleep extension and sleep. This leaves little visible margin for recovery, dinner, hygiene, kit checks, or resolving unexpected pre-departure issues.

There is an unresolved practical transition issue around the Wednesday 13:30-14:30 study followed immediately by the 14:30 physio check described as being at HPC. The calendar commonly shows 30-minute commutes between university and HPC, but no transition is visible here. This is not necessarily impossible, because the study location is not supplied, but it is not substantiated.

The Thursday and Friday competition blocks run 06:30-22:30 on consecutive days, with sleep starting immediately after the Thursday block and another full-day competition beginning immediately after Friday wake-up. That may reflect a team event reality, but the rationale does not discuss meals, decompression, hygiene, injury management, or whether the competition window includes those needs.

The alternatives considered are narrow. The rationale rejects moving Tuesday coffee and using more late Wednesday evening time, but does not show consideration of other ways to reduce the heavy Monday/Tuesday evening study burden or to make the pre-departure Wednesday less brittle.

The proposal deletes Thursday and Friday academic/social commitments and correctly flags that some need justification or confirmation, but the human feasibility of those cancellations remains unresolved; the technical validation only confirms deletion authorization for the training events.
critic_evaluation.feedback: The proposal has a sensible high-level priority structure: national team competition is treated as dominant, protected sleep is mostly respected, packing is placed before departure sleep, and study time is added before missed academic work accumulates. The main human-quality issue is that the plan achieves this by loading five new study hours into an already demanding training-and-class sequence immediately before two consecutive 16-hour competition days. A revision should either make the current distribution more convincingly grounded in the user’s actual capacity and travel logistics, or reconsider the distribution so that study, recovery, packing, and transitions are less compressed. The Proposer should especially recheck whether the Monday and Tuesday 19:00-21:00 study blocks are expected to be effective after afternoon training, whether Wednesday’s study-to-physio transition is physically workable, and whether the Thursday/Friday competition blocks already include meals, transfers, and recovery needs.

plausibility_review.reason: The resulting schedule is technically conflict-free but humanly tight in a way that could significantly affect manageability and the visible goals. The added study blocks are concentrated after long training/class days on Monday and Tuesday, Wednesday has a compressed pre-departure chain with little visible margin and a possible location-transition gap before physio, and the plan enters two consecutive 06:30-22:30 competition days with minimal visible recovery. These are grounded risks rather than objective impossibilities, because the user may be accustomed to this load and some needs may be embedded in team arrangements, but the rationale does not substantiate that.
plausibility_review.suggested_improvement: Reconsider or better justify the workload distribution using the fuller context: confirm whether evening study after training is genuinely usable, whether Wednesday’s transition and packing plan are workable, and whether the competition windows include ordinary meals, travel, and recovery. If not, look for a less brittle distribution rather than simply filling open calendar slots.

critic_evaluation.feedback: The revised proposal responds meaningfully to the prior review. It reduces late-evening study load, protects Wednesday afternoon more convincingly around physio and team briefing, moves packing earlier, and adds an explicit pre-call-up transfer window. As a whole, the visible week is now more balanced than the earlier version. The main remaining human-quality issue is not ordinary calendar conflict but brittleness around Thursday morning: the plan depends on one hour from 05:30 to 06:30 being enough for final preparation and airport transfer before a high-priority national team call-up, and the rationale acknowledges that the route is unknown. The Proposer should either substantiate that this window is workable with the fuller context or reconsider how final prep and transfer margin are represented. The broad 16-hour competition blocks may be realistic for a team event, but they should remain treated as dependent on team-provided meals, recovery, transfers, and end-of-day logistics rather than as proof that personal needs are automatically covered.

plausibility_review.reason: Most prior manageability concerns have been improved, but the Thursday airport call-up remains a concrete potentially consequential weak point. The calendar places sleep until 05:30, then a single 05:30-06:30 block for final prep and airport transfer, followed immediately by a 06:30-22:30 travel-and-competition day. Because the rationale explicitly says airport route feasibility is unknown, this could significantly affect the visible high-priority goal if the window is too short. This is not an objective incompatibility, since the airport may be nearby and preparation may already be mostly complete, but the current proposal does not substantiate that.
plausibility_review.suggested_improvement: Use the fuller context to verify or better justify the Thursday morning logistics, especially whether final preparation and airport transfer can realistically fit before the 06:30 call-up. If that cannot be grounded, reconsider the distribution of final prep and departure margin without assuming that a technically free one-hour slot is sufficient.
